title: GitHub - patch-gg/trompe: Texture a whole game level from a gray blockout with image models: plan cameras, paint, project, bake. Real shadows, glTF out.
html:
@patch_gg · village blockout + FLUX 3 Klein + Fibo 2 · 128 views on fal, $4.44, 26 minutes, one view at a time.

trompe plans cameras where a player can stand, has an image model paint what each one sees, projects every painting back onto the level and bakes one texture. It paints under overcast light, so the texture comes out as albedo and your engine lights it with real shadows. Planning, projection and baking run in your browser on your GPU; the image models run on fal.

Demo video, 42 s · Before and after · Baked shadows vs real light · What the prompts fixed

npm install
export FAL_KEY=your-fal-key                   # used by the dev server's fal proxy
npm run dev                                   # http://localhost:5178

To use it:

  • Pick a sample level (Village, Courtyard, Hall) or drop in your own 
    .glb
    . It needs UVs and Y up.
  • Describe the look you want, as materials ("weathered limestone and ochre plaster walls, terracotta roofs"). Don't name objects: anything named here, like a fountain or a market stall, gets painted onto walls.
  • Press Plan cameras, then Texture level.
  • Download the textured 
    .glb
    or the texture.

If you leave the fal key field empty, the dev server adds 

FAL_KEY
server-side and the browser never sees it. A key typed into the field is kept in that browser and sent straight to fal.

Headless, from the command line, the run is saved to 

runs/<id>/
:

node scripts/texture.mjs --level samples/village.glb --id village --views 90 --spacing 3.5 --aerial 8 --roofs 24 --holes 12 \
  --atlas 8192 --style "a sunlit Mediterranean hill village: weathered limestone and ochre plaster walls, ..."

To try prompt or model changes cheaply before a full run, 

scripts/prompt-test.mjs
repaints chosen views of a saved run, with the texture rebuilt up to just before each one. It can also paint roof passes on top of the finished run, and it saves every image to 
runs/<run>-ab/<tag>/
. 
--dry
writes the prompts and inputs without calling any model.

To fill whatever a saved run still misses, 

--resume <id>
plans views only where the texture is missing or poor and paints on top, in place. For example: 
node scripts/texture.mjs --level samples/village.glb --resume village --views 30 --aerial 8 --atlas 8192
. 
--parallel 6
paints non-overlapping views at the same time, which is faster but leaves visible seams where they meet.

On WSL2, 

scripts/browser.mjs
points headless Chromium's ANGLE at Mesa's D3D12 driver, so runs use the real GPU instead of SwiftShader.

StepWhereWhat
Plan
src/core/planner.ts
 Sample walkable floors at eye height. Drop spots inside solids or out in the open (rooftops). Join spots a player can walk between (following the floor, so stairs count) and keep the play areas. Render cheap probes from 8 headings per spot, then pick cameras greedily until most reachable surface is captured well. Each camera is ordered to overlap what's already painted. Roofs get their own close, drone-style cameras (
--roofs
, 15 m out, 50° down, facing each slope), chosen the same way over roof surfaces only. Then 
--aerial
cameras pick up what's left, with their own budget: a high ring looks down at the tops of props and the ground behind them, and a low ring outside the level faces the outer walls. Paint order: players' views, then roofs, then the rings. Last, a hole pass (
--holes
) looks for texels nothing has painted (ground hidden behind props from eye height, tops of props). It renders candidate cameras 5 m above where players stand, plus the high ring, and picks them by how many unpainted pixels each actually sees. Those views paint only the holes.
See
src/core/clay.ts
, 
views.ts
 Lit gray render per camera (sky light, a soft key light, screen-space AO), plus per-pixel position, normal and UV buffers. The "state" image is the clay render with already-painted texture composited in. By default the clay is lit like an overcast day, with no cast shadows, and the prompts ask for soft overcast light. That's why photogrammetry is shot under cloud: the texture comes out close to albedo. 
--lighting outdoor
paints under a sun and bakes its shadows in. It looks photographic from that one sun, but each view paints the shadows a little differently, and they can't be relit.
Prompt
src/core/semantics.ts
, 
src/providers/models.ts
 Each view's prompt is built from the level's part names (glTF material names, else mesh names). It lists the parts in the area to paint with rough positions ("house walls (left), stone stairs (bottom)"). Flat details such as windows, doors and stonework are allowed, but nothing may stick out or be added (awnings, stalls, signs, lamps and so on) unless the level models it. The look is materials only. Roof views get a roof-tile prompt, a mask covering only the roofs, and project nothing else.
Paint
src/providers/
 The first view, and any view that's over 75% unpainted, goes to FLUX 3 Klein ($0.009). It keeps the geometry far better than Fibo on blank views. Everything else is a masked fill with Fibo 2 Edit ($0.04), and so is every roof view. Views with under 3% unpainted are skipped. Views run one at a time, so each sees everything painted before it.
Paste
src/core/composite.ts
 Known pixels are kept exactly. The new image's colours are shifted by how far the model drifted on the known pixels along the seam (a push-pull fill of that difference, fading over ~120 px), then it fades in over 10 px. Any part of the area the model hands back unchanged (still gray clay) is left out of the projection, so the gray never passes for paint and a later view or the hole pass gets another go at it.
Project
src/core/atlas.ts
 A UV-space pass writes colour into each texel this camera sees better than whatever is stored. Quality is cos(angle)/distance, and pixels within 6 px of a silhouette count at 0.3x, so a better view replaces them. Texels captured at under 0.4x a later view's quality get regenerated. A view can be limited to some of its pixels (transparent, premultiplied); roof passes use this.
Light
src/core/viewer.ts
 The Lit display mode uses the texture as albedo under a real sun with shadow maps and sky light, so shadows always match the geometry. The sun sliders move them live. The Textured mode shows the texture as painted.
Bake
src/core/export.ts
 The texture is the bake: gutters are padded, then it's exported as glTF. An overcast (albedo) texture goes on a lit material for the engine to light; a sun-painted one goes on an unlit material.

The demo level (

samples/build_village.py
) names its parts through glTF materials ("house walls", "tiled roof", "stone stairs", "wooden barrels", ...), which is what the prompts read. It also unwraps by importance: surfaces players walk past get 62% of the texture, roofs 14% and outer walls 6%. Levels without part names still work: roofs are found by slope and height, and prompts go without a parts list.

The AI sky backdrop averages sky pixels only from views whose model painted the whole frame (Klein). Masked fills leave the clay sky as it was.

The village in the video is run 

village-07
: 128 views, $4.44 and 26 minutes on fal, painted one view at a time under overcast light. 88 views come from where players stand, 20 from over the roofs, 11 from around the outside and 9 fill holes. It's shown lit by a real sun, which swings round in the last shot.

src/demo.ts
and 
scripts/capture.mjs
replay a saved run wave by wave and render the frames straight off the WebGL canvas. 
video/compose.py
lays them out in Patch's video style (
video/lightsdown.py
): the clip in a plain frame with the pink patch on its corner, one caption line under it, the label beside it. 
video/audio.py
mixes the score and UI sounds, and 
video/encode.sh
muxes the result. 
docs/readme/make_art.py
draws this README's header and footer.

The layout uses Patch's brand kit, which isn't in this repo: Patch Pixel is Patch's own typeface. Put the kit at 

./brand-kit
(or point 
PATCH_BRAND_KIT
at it) to rebuild the video or the README art.

npm test          # unit tests for compositing and planner helpers
npm run build     # type check + production build
  • Resolution. Views are 1024 px. Klein can paint 2048 px views for $0.014 and shows visibly more detail; Fibo works at about 1 megapixel either way. 
    --view-size 2048
    works, but a full run then keeps about 8 GB of per-view images in the tab. Views need to stream to disk as they finish first.
  • Some outer walls stay gray. Walls facing narrow gaps between buildings aren't seen well by any camera yet.
  • Misprojections. Overhangs (like the arcade ceiling) can catch misprojected fragments, and gables sometimes get a patch of painted sky. Next is an automatic retouch pass: find seams and odd patches, then send masked fills over them.
  • Floor clutter from down-looking views. Floor views make the models paint crates and debris onto the ground, so they're off (
    downYaws: 0
    ). Floor views need their own prompt, or the normals check from the spike.
  • No local models yet. fal only so far; a ComfyUI provider is next.
  • Albedo is approximate. Overcast painting removes cast shadows, but the models still paint some soft shading and contact darkening. Dividing out the known clay shading, or a Marigold-style intrinsic decomposition, would get closer. Normal and roughness maps are planned too.
  • No UV unwrapping. Levels must come with UVs; importance weighting only exists in the demo level's builder.

Apache-2.0, see LICENSE. The Patch name, mark, wordmark and Patch Pixel belong to Patch and aren't covered by it. Funnel Sans and Red Hat Mono in 

video/fonts/
are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (OFL-FunnelSans.txt, OFL-RedHatMono.txt).

The demo video's music isn't in the repo. To rebuild the video with a score, put a track at 

video/audio/music.mp3
and its downbeats in 
video/audio/beats.json
; without one, 
video/audio.py
mixes the UI sounds alone.

Made by Patch (@patch_gg). Image models run on fal: FLUX 3 Klein by Black Forest Labs for first views, Fibo 2 Edit by Bria for fills and roofs (others are wired up in 

src/providers/models.ts
). Built on three.js, three-mesh-bvh, Vite and Playwright.

title_zh: trompe,使用图像模型从灰色遮挡纹理整个游戏关卡,下载trompe的源码_GitHub_帮酷真实阴影，glTF 输出。
html_zh:
@patch_gg · Village blockout + FLUX 3 Klein + Fibo 2 · fal 上有 128 次观看，4.44 美元，26 分钟，一次观看一个。

trompe 将摄像机设计在玩家可以站立的位置，让图像模型绘制每个人看到的内容，将每幅画投影回关卡上并烘焙一个纹理。它在阴光下绘制，因此纹理以反照率的形式出现，并且您的引擎用真实的阴影照亮它。规划、投影和烘焙在 GPU 上的浏览​​器中运行；图像模型在fal上运行。

演示视频，42 秒·之前和之后·烘焙阴影与真实光线·提示修复了什么

npm install
export FAL_KEY=your-fal-key                   # used by the dev server's fal proxy
npm run dev                                   # http://localhost:5178

使用方法：

  • 选择一个示例级别（村庄、庭院、大厅）或放入您自己的级别
    .glb
    。它需要 UV 和 Y 向上。
  • 描述您想要的外观，作为材料（“风化的石灰石和赭色石膏墙，赤土屋顶”）。不要命名物体：这里命名的任何东西，比如喷泉或市场摊位，都会被画在墙上。
  • 按“计划相机”，然后按“纹理级别”。
  • 下载有纹理的
    .glb
    或纹理。

如果将 fal 键字段留空，开发服务器会添加

FAL_KEY
服务器端和浏览器永远不会看到它。在该字段中输入的密钥将保存在该浏览器中并直接发送到 fal。

无头，从命令行，运行被保存到

runs/<id>/
:

node scripts/texture.mjs --level samples/village.glb --id village --views 90 --spacing 3.5 --aerial 8 --roofs 24 --holes 12 \
  --atlas 8192 --style "a sunlit Mediterranean hill village: weathered limestone and ochre plaster walls, ..."

要在完整运行之前以较低的成本尝试提示或模型更改，

scripts/prompt-test.mjs
重新绘制已保存运行的选定视图，并在每个视图之前重建纹理。它还可以在完成的运行顶部绘制屋顶通道，并将每个图像保存到
runs/<run>-ab/<tag>/
. 
--dry
编写提示和输入而不调用任何模型。

为了填补已保存的跑步仍然遗漏的任何内容，

--resume <id>
仅在纹理缺失或较差的地方规划视图，并在顶部就位绘制。例如：
node scripts/texture.mjs --level samples/village.glb --resume village --views 30 --aerial 8 --atlas 8192
. 
--parallel 6
同时绘制不重叠的视图，速度更快，但会在它们相交的地方留下可见的接缝。

在 WSL2 上，

scripts/browser.mjs
将无头 Chromium 的 ANGLE 指向 Mesa 的 D3D12 驱动程序，因此运行时使用真正的 GPU 而不是 SwiftShader。

步在哪里什么
计划
src/core/planner.ts
 在视线高度处采样适合步行的地板。将点滴在固体内部或露天（屋顶）。连接玩家可以在其之间行走的点（沿着地板，因此楼梯也算在内）并保留游戏区域。从每个点 8 个航向渲染廉价探针，然后贪婪地挑选相机，直到捕捉到最可到达的表面。每个摄像机都被命令与已经绘制的内容重叠。屋顶有自己的近距离无人机式摄像机（
 --屋顶
，向外 15 m，向下 50°，面向每个斜坡），仅在屋顶表面上选择相同的方式。然后
 - 天线
摄像机根据自己的预算拍摄剩下的内容：一个高环俯视道具的顶部及其后面的地面，而关卡外的一个低环面向外墙。绘制顺序：玩家视野，然后是屋顶，然后是圆环。最后，一洞传球（
 --孔
）寻找没有绘制任何内容的纹理像素（从眼睛高度隐藏在道具后面的地面，道具的顶部）。它将候选摄像机渲染到玩家站立位置上方 5 m 处，加上高环，并根据每个摄像机实际看到的未绘制像素数来选择它们。这些观点只描绘了漏洞。
看
src/core/clay.ts
,
视图.ts
 每个相机的亮灰色渲染（天空光、软键光、屏幕空间 AO），以及每像素位置、法线和 UV 缓冲区。 “状态”图像是已合成纹理的粘土渲染。默认情况下，粘土像阴天一样照亮，没有投射阴影，并且提示要求柔和的阴光。这就是摄影测量在云下拍摄的原因：纹理接近反照率。
 --室外照明
在太阳下绘画并将其阴影融入其中。从那个太阳看来，它看起来很像照片，但每个视图绘制的阴影都略有不同，而且它们无法重新照亮。
迅速的
src/core/semantics.ts
,
 src/providers/models.ts
 每个视图的提示都是根据关卡的零件名称（glTF 材质名称，其他网格名称）构建的。它列出了该区域中要绘制的部分的大致位置（“房屋墙壁（左），石楼梯（底部）”）。允许使用窗户、门和石雕等平面细节，但任何内容都不得突出或添加（遮阳篷、摊位、标志、灯等），除非关卡对其进行建模。外观仅是材料。屋顶视图会出现屋顶瓦片提示，一个仅覆盖屋顶的遮罩，不会投射任何其他内容。
画
src/提供者/
 第一个视图以及任何超过 75% 未绘制的视图将授予 FLUX 3 Klein（0.009 美元）。它在空白视图上保持几何图形的效果比 Fibo 好得多。其他一切都是使用 Fibo 2 Edit（0.04 美元）进行蒙版填充，每个屋顶视图也是如此。未绘制部分低于 3% 的视图将被跳过。视图一次运行一个，因此每个视图都会看到之前绘制的所有内容。
粘贴
src/core/composite.ts
 已知像素被准确保留。新图像的颜色会根据模型在沿接缝的已知像素上漂移的距离而发生变化（该差异的推拉填充，淡出约 120 像素），然后淡出超过 10 像素。模型交还给原样的区域的任何部分（仍然是灰色粘土）都被排除在投影之外，因此灰色永远不会通过油漆，并且稍后的视图或孔通行证会再次尝试。
项目
src/core/atlas.ts
 UV 空间通道将颜色写入相机看到的每个纹素中，比存储的颜色更好。质量为 cos（角度）/距离，轮廓 6 像素内的像素计数为 0.3x，因此更好的视图会取代它们。以低于 0.4xa 的后期视图质量捕获的纹理像素会重新生成。视图可以限制为其某些像素（透明、预乘）；屋顶通行证使用这个。
光
src/core/viewer.ts
 光照显示模式使用纹理作为真实阳光下的反照率，并带有阴影贴图和天空光，因此阴影始终与几何体匹配。太阳滑块使它们活动。纹理模式显示绘制时的纹理。
烤
src/core/export.ts
 纹理是烘焙的：填充排水沟，然后将其导出为 glTF。阴天（反照率）纹理出现在照亮的材质上，以便引擎照亮；太阳涂漆的材料是在未发光的材料上。

演示级别（

samples/build_village.py
）通过 glTF 材质命名其各个部分（“房屋墙壁”、“瓦片屋顶”、“石楼梯”、“木桶”……），这就是提示所读的内容。它还按重要性展开：玩家走过的表面获得 62% 的纹理，屋顶 14%，外墙 6%。没有零件名称的关卡仍然有效：屋顶是通过坡度和高度找到的，并且提示没有零件列表。

AI 天空背景仅对模型绘制整个帧的视图中的天空像素进行平均 (Klein)。蒙版填充使粘土天空保持原样。

summary_zh: 开源项目 trompe 能用图像模型给灰色白模关卡整体上贴图：自动规划玩家可站立位置的相机视角，让图像模型绘制每个视角，再把画面投影回关卡并烘焙成一张贴图，输出 glTF。示例村庄关卡用 FLUX 3 Klein 和 Fibo 2 在 fal 上跑 128 个视角，花费 4.44 美元、26 分钟。它在阴天光照下绘制，得到的是反照率贴图，可由游戏引擎打真实阴影；规划、投影和烘焙在浏览器本地 GPU 上完成，也支持命令行批量运行和低成本提示词 A/B 测试。
